claim.property: System hosts-file integrity and fail-closed mutation on initial read failure; truthful manual-sync verification failures
claim.attacker: A lower-privilege local principal able to invoke the CLI or influence route state, or a remote/browser principal attempting to trigger privileged sync. Filesystem read/write failures themselves are not assumed attacker-controlled.
claim.scope: Exact-head change and commit message: reject unreadable hosts files before mutation, distinguish them from readable empty files, reject unreadable post-write verification, reconcile empty route sets, and preserve existing elevation/error paths and best-effort inspection.
claim.limitations: Not a claim of transactional writes, arbitrary malformed-marker repair, complete-file post-write equality, safe recovery from route-store read failures, or a newly designed privilege/authentication boundary.

assets: Unmanaged system/custom hosts mappings and managed route mappings
OS authorization to modify system hosts and execute an elevated CLI
Accuracy of manual sync/cleanup success and failure reporting

principals.name: Local operator
principals.existing_authority: Runs installed CLI and controls its own environment and user-owned state. Writing system hosts requires existing filesystem authority or OS-approved elevation.

principals.name: Privileged CLI/proxy
principals.existing_authority: May rewrite system hosts when started with sufficient privileges. This authority exists at the merge base.

principals.name: Route-state writer
principals.existing_authority: Can alter route data only where filesystem permissions already allow it. The existing daemon already consumes that data; this PR adds no route-input channel.

principals.name: Remote/browser principal or unrelated local user
principals.existing_authority: May reach the proxy subject to binding/network constraints, but has no presumed state-file write permission, sync token, system-hosts write permission, or sudo authorization.

observations.title: Read-failure integrity guard is effective; no supported new vulnerability
prerequisites: Initial hosts read throws, including unreadable or absent files; or post-write verification read throws

chain.capability: A failure is injected at the filesystem seam. No evidence establishes that a lower-trust attacker can induce that failure on the real protected file.
chain.reachability: Both mutation helpers and the manual handler use the new read result; daemon sync reaches the same helper.
chain.control: Neither request input nor route data can turn null into a successful read.
chain.boundary: Initial failure returns false before write; manual root/Windows paths report failure and non-root Unix retains OS-mediated elevation.
chain.impact: Zero initial-read-failure writes at head; populated sync at base attempted a write. Empty-sync unreadable verification changes from false success at base to false at head. No new attacker authority demonstrated.

observations.confidence: high for source behavior and mocked boundary; no real OS exploitation claim
observations.merge_relevance: Supports the bounded security claim; not a vulnerability blocker.

observations.title: No privilege-boundary widening established
prerequisites: Local CLI invocation or a request to the existing sync endpoint
OS-granted elevation remains necessary where hosts is not writable

chain.capability: Local callers already execute their own CLI; network callers do not thereby gain route-state control or elevation.
chain.reachability: Read failures now use preexisting CLI failure/elevation branches. Remote callback authentication and route-loading code are unchanged.
chain.control: Elevation arguments retain existing fixed executable/subcommands and PORTLESS_* forwarding. Callback loads local routes, not request-provided hostnames.
chain.boundary: Existing sudo authorization and endpoint token/origin/peer checks remain in place.
chain.impact: Additional authorized retry on read failure is not evidence of a new cross-user/root capability. No token or other secret was accessed.

observations.confidence: high for delta; runtime OS authorization untested by design
evidence: git base/head diff: routes.ts, cli-utils.ts, proxy.ts, hosts-sync-auth.ts unchanged
observations.merge_relevance: No security blocker; not a broad audit of existing state-directory trust.

observations.title: Inherited integrity/reconciliation limitations are not fixed by this change
prerequisites: Malformed orphan marker, a write producing empty/truncated content, or route-store read failure

chain.capability: Synthetic malformed data/I/O failures; attacker control over real protected-file faults is unestablished.
chain.reachability: Existing block parser, non-transactional writer, and RouteStore empty-on-error behavior feed sync at both base and head.
chain.control: The probe controls only memory fixtures. This does not demonstrate an attacker crossing OS file permissions.
chain.boundary: No new boundary crossing. Existing helpers conflate missing/malformed blocks, verify managed content only, and consume empty routes on route-read error.
chain.impact: An orphan block can remain after an empty sync; empty post-write content satisfies an empty desired set even if unrelated entries were lost; unreadable route data clears valid managed entries. Each reproduced at the actual merge base as well as head.

observations.confidence: high for inherited correctness behavior; no exploitability claim
observations.merge_relevance: Route to correctness follow-up, not an in-scope security regression or adjacent exploitable blocker.
